description: GazFlow is a gas-network simulation application with pressure-holding studies, map and schematic views, contingency analysis and export workflows. Its README describes a GasLib-11 demonstration and separate validation documentation. The provider is Improba. Coverage: The application models user-defined gas networks; the included demonstration is a benchmark, not a measured service area. Time and spatial detail depend on configuration. Access: A public repository exposes the project and README. No code, dependency or application was executed. Licence and cost: The GazFlow Public License permits free individual and noncommercial academic use but requires an agreement for enterprise use. It explicitly states that it is not an OSI open-source licence. Limitations: The commercial-licence document is a nonbinding draft. GazFlow is a comparative study tool, not certified for real-time network operation or safety-critical decisions. For simulation it may support exploratory pressure and capacity studies once the documented validation claims are checked. Related resources: The README explicitly names GasLib-11. The existing data-gaslib record covers that benchmark family.
